input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 is the only covenant in the Agreement that restrains our side (Section 6.3 restrains HDI, and for two years post-term, which favours us). It sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred "no restriction" position, and so is not redlined: (i) it runs "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail, and the term under Section 4.1 is one year (auto-renewing, terminable on 90 days' notice), so the restraint never exceeds 12 months without our consent to renew; (ii) scope is limited by product and channel — Internet projects similar to the Site offering Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, with the competing products named (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) — rather than the walk-away formulation of "any competing business"; and (iii) there is a carve-out in Section 6.2 for a closeout-merchandise site, and "Deerskin Products" itself excludes closeout goods and the Joan Cook Catalog. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted only: there is no express carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (so acquiring a leather retailer that runs a competing site could implicate 6.1), and the words "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" are looser than a purely named-product limit. We would take these as clarifications if the document is reopened for other reasons, but they are not material enough to breach the fallback, and deletion of 6.1 would be disproportionate given HDI's heavier reciprocal restraint in Section 6.3.
